survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 creative thinking results for Uzbekistan using the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA design is a complex, multi-stage sampling of schools and students, and OECD estimates are produced to reflect that design (including uncertainty intervals shown in the figures). The factsheet does not specify the exact student weight variable name(s) or whether replicate weights were used, so analysts should follow the OECD PISA 2022 Database guidance for variance estimation and weighting. Because this is a descriptive reporting factsheet (not an ML modeling paper), the appropriate approach is to use the OECD-provided weights/replication scheme when reproducing estimates, rather than applying custom ML-style weighting.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values handling is not applicable here because the factsheet is a descriptive results summary of PISA 2022 creative thinking proficiency and related percentages/relative differences, rather than an analysis that explicitly models PV-based achievement with a documented PV-combining procedure. Missing-data handling is not reported in the factsheet because it focuses on published OECD estimates and does not describe the microdata imputation/exclusion rules used during OECD scaling and estimation. This omission is therefore a reporting scope limitation of the factsheet rather than a transparency gap about an author-run ML pipeline.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample for Uzbekistan consists of 7,293 students in 202 schools who completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science, representing about 482,100 15-year-olds in Uzbekistan (estimated 88% of the total 15-year-old population). The factsheet does not further describe additional exclusions (e.g., missing background questionnaire items) or task-level completion filters; it reports OECD’s published estimates for the PISA 2022 creative thinking test.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III (Creative Minds, Creative Schools) factsheet summarizes creative thinking performance for 15-year-old students in Uzbekistan. PISA 2022 implemented a creative thinking cognitive test in 64 countries/economies (including Uzbekistan), with 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes: generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating and improving ideas, across four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, scientific problem solving). Uzbekistan’s mean creative thinking score is 14 on a 60-point scale, significantly below the OECD average (33). Only 16% of students reach Level 3 (baseline proficiency), and 2% are top performers at Levels 5–6. The factsheet also reports within-country gaps: socio-economic status predicts creative thinking (2% of variation explained in Uzbekistan), girls outperform boys by 1.7 points, and students’ beliefs/attitudes (e.g., openness to creativity and fixed mindset) are associated with performance. Results are presented with uncertainty intervals and include cautions for some comparison countries due to PISA sampling standards.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is an OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet rather than an empirical ML study. It reports descriptive international comparisons and proficiency distributions derived from OECD’s scaling and estimation procedures, but it does not specify an author-run predictive model, algorithmic pipeline, or target-variable-specific ML metrics. Consequently, fields related to ML techniques, main findings as model outputs, and conceptual confounders for a predictive framework are intentionally left empty because the factsheet does not conduct new statistical/ML estimation beyond presenting published results.
